slides.title: Concurrency
slides.main: First find what is slow: computation or waiting — it decides the tool.

items.title: Locking
items.sub: Threads don't speed up pure computation

body.text: Concurrency — tasks interleaved; parallelism — at once on different cores.

slides.title: Threads
slides.main: Waits overlap: three threads of 0.2 s take about 0.2 s, not 0.6.

body.text:
import threading
import time

results = []

def work(name):
    time.sleep(0.2)
    results.append(name)

start = time.perf_counter()
threads = [threading.Thread(target=work, args=(n,)) for n in "abc"]
for t in threads:
    t.start()
for t in threads:
    t.join()
print(sorted(results), time.perf_counter() - start < 0.5)

slides.title: Race and Lock
slides.sub: Shared memory is a source of trouble
slides.main: Take the lock via with: it is released even if an error occurs inside.

body.text:
import threading

count = 0
lock = threading.Lock()

def inc(n):
    global count
    for _ in range(n):
        with lock:
            count += 1

threads = [threading.Thread(target=inc, args=(50000,)) for _ in range(4)]
for t in threads:
    t.start()
for t in threads:
    t.join()
print(count)
Without the lock the result would be smaller and different every time: read-add-write is not indivisible.

slides.title: GIL
slides.main: The GIL is released on waiting: threads for I/O, processes for computation.

slides.title: ThreadPoolExecutor
slides.main: A task's exception is kept in the future and raised when the result is read.

body.text:
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
import time

def fetch(n):
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return n * n

def boom():
    raise ValueError("failure")

with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:
    print(list(pool.map(fetch, [1, 2, 3, 4])))
    futures = [pool.submit(fetch, n) for n in (5, 6)]
    print(sorted(f.result() for f in as_completed(futures)))
    try:
        pool.submit(boom).result()
    except ValueError as e:
        print("from the thread:", e)

slides.title: Queues
slides.main: A queue is thread-safe: less shared state, fewer races.

body.text:
import queue
import threading

q = queue.Queue()
results = []

def consumer():
    while True:
        item = q.get()
        if item is None:          # stop signal
            break
        results.append(item * 2)

t = threading.Thread(target=consumer)
t.start()
for i in range(5):
    q.put(i)
q.put(None)
t.join()
print(results)

slides.title: Event and Semaphore
slides.main: Never wait forever: waits have a timeout.

body.text:
import threading
import time

stop = threading.Event()
ticks = []

def worker():
    while not stop.is_set():
        ticks.append(1)
        stop.wait(0.05)

t = threading.Thread(target=worker)
t.start()
time.sleep(0.2)
stop.set()
t.join()
print(len(ticks) >= 2, stop.is_set())

sem = threading.Semaphore(2)
print(sem.acquire(), sem.acquire(), sem.acquire(timeout=0.05))

slides.title: Thread details
slides.main: A thread can't be stopped from outside — only asked via an Event.

body.text:
import threading

local = threading.local()

def work(n):
    local.value = n
    print(local.value, threading.current_thread().name)

t = threading.Thread(target=work, args=(7,), name="worker")
t.start()
t.join()
print(hasattr(local, "value"))
daemon=True — the thread doesn't block program exit; ordinary threads are waited for.

slides.title: How to choose
slides.main: Most often a thread pool for the network and a process pool for calculations is enough.

cells.title: How many at once?
cells.sub: dozens → threads; thousands of connections → asyncio

cells.title: Need shared memory?
cells.sub: threads — yes; processes — no, data is copied

slides.title: Measure
slides.main: Amdahl's law: the indivisible part limits the gain; for small jobs a pool does harm.

body.text:
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

def request(_):
    time.sleep(0.1)

t0 = time.perf_counter()
for i in range(10):
    request(i)
seq = time.perf_counter() - t0

t0 = time.perf_counter()
with ThreadPoolExecutor(10) as pool:
    list(pool.map(request, range(10)))
par = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(seq > 0.9, par < 0.5, seq / par > 3)

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.sub: A thread's exception doesn't reach the main one
slides.main: Without a future a thread's error is only printed — and you may miss it.

body.text:
import threading

def broken():
    raise ValueError("failure")

t = threading.Thread(target=broken)
t.start()
t.join()
print("main thread survived:", t.is_alive())
